title: My 2026 Desk Setup Tour
creator: Sam Whitlock
description:
The desk I work, edit and game at every day, and everything I changed this year.

This video is sponsored by Ledgerline and Corkboard.
Ledgerline: file your taxes free with code SAM at https://ledgerline.com
Corkboard: 6 months of Pro free at https://corkboard.so/sam

Full gear list in the pinned comment.

sentences.t: It's that time of year again, so welcome to my desk setup tour for twenty twenty six.
A lot changed this year, mostly because I moved to a smaller room, so everything had to get more compact.
Let's start with the desk itself.
It's a sit stand desk, a hundred and forty centimeters wide, which is smaller than my old one, but it actually fits the room now.
I stand for maybe two hours a day, usually during calls, because it stops me from slouching.
The top is just a cheap birch plywood sheet that I oiled myself, and it's held up really well.
On top I've got one monitor now instead of two.
It's a thirty four inch ultrawide, and honestly I don't miss the second screen at all, I just split this one in half.
It sits on a monitor arm, so the whole desk surface underneath is free.
Okay, this video has two sponsors, so let me get them both out of the way before the rest of the tour.
First up is Ledgerline, which is how I did my taxes this year.
If you've got freelance income on top of a regular job, like I do, Ledgerline walks you through everything with plain questions instead of tax jargon.
It pulls in your documents automatically, finds deductions for things like your home office, and a real tax expert reviews it if you want.
Simple returns are free, and code SAM gets you twenty five percent off the paid tiers at ledgerline.com.
And my second sponsor is Corkboard, which is the notes app I've basically moved my whole life into.
Video ideas, scripts, shopping lists, client notes, all of it lives there and syncs to every device instantly.
The thing I love is the board view, where I drag notes around like sticky notes, which is how I plan every video now.
It works offline, it's fast, and you can share a board with other people.
Head to corkboard.so/sam for six months of Corkboard Pro for free.
Okay, back to the desk.
My keyboard this year is a seventy five percent board with tactile switches, and I finally stopped buying new keyboards every two months.
Okay, mostly stopped.
The mouse is a lightweight wireless one, nothing fancy, but the battery lasts weeks.
Under everything is a big felt desk mat, mainly because it makes the desk quieter when I type.
For audio, I've got a dynamic microphone on a low profile arm, so it doesn't block the monitor.
And small bookshelf speakers on stands, angled at my ears, for music while I edit.
For calls and recording I use this webcam, mounted on a small arm above the monitor.
Lighting was the biggest upgrade this year.
I added a light bar on top of the monitor that lights the desk without glare on the screen.
And behind the desk there's a strip of warm LEDs, so the wall isn't just a black void on camera.
Cable management, which everyone asks about, is a tray screwed under the desk, a power strip inside it, and a whole lot of velcro ties.
Only one cable goes down to the wall, and it has enough slack for the desk to go all the way up.
The computer is a small form factor PC that sits on a shelf under the desk, so my feet have room.
And finally, the most important item on the desk, a plant that somehow I haven't killed yet.
Its name is Kevin.
So that's the setup for this year, smaller, cleaner, and honestly way nicer to work at.
Tell me what your desk looks like in the comments, and what you'd change about mine.
See you in the next one.
